transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

I came in because I seem to worry about everything lately—my clients, the market, my family, money, even whether moving to the condo was the right decision. It feels like it’s more than the situations really call for.
About how long have you been feeling this level of worry?
About a year and two months now. It really started after I sold my longtime house and moved into the condo.
Do you find it difficult to control or stop the worrying once it starts?
Yes. I’ll tell myself, “Parin, this isn’t urgent,” but then one worry turns into another. Before I know it, I’ve spent half an hour going over little details I meant to let go.
Aside from the worry, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or hopeless?
I wouldn’t say I’ve been persistently sad or hopeless. Mostly it’s the worrying that gets to me.
Do you often find yourself feeling restless or on edge?
I’m not sure I’d say restless, exactly. I do get caught up in my thoughts, but I haven’t really noticed feeling physically on edge.
Have you been having trouble with your sleep?

Most nights, yes. I get into bed at a reasonable time, but then I start going over condo fees, tomorrow’s showings, or whether I missed something in a contract. It takes me a while to settle down, and I wake up feeling like I didn’t fully rest.
Have you noticed any physical tension or soreness in your muscles, such as in your neck, shoulders, or back?
Yes. By the end of the day, my neck and shoulders feel tight, like I’ve been bracing myself. And sometimes I notice I’m clenching my jaw when I’m driving between listings or sitting at my desk.
Have you found that you get fatigued or tired more easily than usual?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I do feel worn out some days, but I haven’t noticed that I’m getting tired more easily than usual.
Have you had trouble concentrating or noticed your mind going blank because of the worry?
Yes. When I’m reviewing purchase agreements or inspection addendums, I’ll sometimes read the same paragraph three or four times. A worry pops into my head and I lose track of what I was checking.

latest_inference.note: Patient confirmed difficulty concentrating, completing the requirement of at least three associated symptoms (sleep disturbance, muscle tension, concentration impairment) alongside uncontrollable, generalized worry lasting over six months, confirming Generalized Anxiety Disorder and ruling out unspecified anxiety disorder.
